From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Esprit

English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
esprit
Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French esprit (“spirit”). Doublet of spirit, spiritus, spirytus, sprite, and spright, possibly also spree.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ɛsˈpɹiː/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • Rhymes: -iː

Noun

[edit]

esprit (uncountable)

  1. Spirit, enthusiasm.
  2. A wit.
  3. Liveliness, or active mind and spirit.

Related terms

[edit]
  • bel esprit
  • esprit de corps
  • l'esprit de l'escalier

Translations

[edit]
spirit, enthusiasm
  • Bulgarian: дух (bg) m (duh)
  • Finnish: henki (fi), henkevyys (fi)
  • German: Esprit (de) m
  • Romanian: spirit (ro) n
  • Russian: дух (ru) m (dux), энтузиа́зм (ru) m (entuziázm)
wit
  • Bulgarian: ум (bg) m (um), интелигентност (bg) f (inteligentnost)
  • Finnish: henkevyys (fi), älykkyys (fi)
liveliness, or active mind and spirit
  • Finnish: henkevyys (fi), eloisuus (fi)
  • German: Esprit (de) m
  • Russian: жи́вость (ru) f (žívostʹ)

References

[edit]
  • “esprit”, in Webster’s Revised Unabridged Dictionary, Springfield, Mass.: G. & C. Merriam, 1913, →OCLC.

[edit]
  • Pitres, Presti, Priest, Sprite, pierst, priest, re-tips, respit, retips, ripest, sitrep, sprite, stripe, tripes

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Middle French esperit, from Old French, borrowed from Latin spiritus through Ecclesiastical Latin and Christian religious texts.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ɛs.pʁi/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Canada (Shawinigan)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Paris)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Toulouse)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

esprit m (plural esprits)

  1. immaterial or incorporeal substance
  2. disembodied mind
  3. mind (in the wide sense)
  4. mind (as principle of thought)
  5. specific mind aptitude
  6. high mind aptitude
  7. deep intention, sense, or purpose (of a text, action, attitude...); philosophy (in figurative sense)
  8. (metonymic) human being, as possessing abilities of mind
  9. (archaic) volatile fluid, especially alcohol
